The Problem

Pakistan's energy deals are harder than they should be.

Circular debt, a single-buyer market, and NEPRA's shift to net billing have made solar and storage projects slower to trust and harder to finance — for buyers and EPCs alike.

Slow, Manual Process

Buyers contact suppliers one by one, by phone and email, with no standardized way to compare bids.

Hard to Verify

Supplier track records, licensing, and delivery history are difficult for a single buyer to check alone.

Financing Starts From Zero

Banks and funds re-run diligence on every deal because there's no shared, verified data to work from.

Why EEMMIC

The traditional way, versus the EEMMIC way.

EEMMIC is designed to replace scattered phone calls and manual verification with one connected, verified process.

Who We Are

The platform built for Pakistan's energy transition.

EEMMIC exists to make Pakistan's B2B and captive solar market easier to trust. We verify buyers' load and site data, vet EPC suppliers' track records, confirm deal structures against NEPRA's net-billing rules, and connect qualified financing — so a deal moves on facts, not sales calls.

Verification-Led

Every supplier and deal is checked against real track records and regulatory rules before it moves forward.

Sustainability First

Every deal we coordinate is measured against its environmental impact, not just its price.

The Process

How EEMMIC Works

Four stages that turn a solar or storage inquiry into a financed, verified, monitored deal.

Stage 1

Evaluation

Buyer · Supplier · Regulatory

We verify the buyer's load, the supplier's track record, and the deal's legality under NEPRA's net-billing rules before anyone bids.

Stage 2

Management

Delivery · Compliance

Milestones, documentation, and DISCO interconnection paperwork are tracked centrally, not chased by phone and email.

Stage 3

Marketplace

Competing Bids

Qualified EPCs bid on a verified requirement — price, timeline, equipment, and warranty compared side by side.

Stage 4

Investment

Financing the Deal

Banks and infrastructure funds review the same verified data EEMMIC used at evaluation — reducing their own diligence cost.
